heading: About
lead: I am an undergraduate researcher at IIIT Hyderabad working at the intersection of robotics, computer vision, and language systems.
bio: I am a BTech + MS student in Electronics and Communication Engineering at the International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad, and an undergraduate researcher at the Robotics Research Center under Prof. Sourav Garg.

My work centres on embodied perception: how an agent builds a representation of a space it has never seen, and how language can be grounded in that representation well enough to act on. In practice that means vision-language models paired with topological graph structure for navigation, feedforward 3D mapping for reconstruction, and 3D-vision-plus-RL policies for dexterous manipulation on a LEAP Hand.

Alongside the robotics work I build LLM systems — routing, evaluation, and safety pipelines — and study multi-agent reinforcement learning where reward misalignment is the interesting failure mode rather than an inconvenience.
motivation: I am drawn to problems where a system has to commit to a decision under genuine uncertainty about the world — a robot that must move before it has mapped the room, a router that must choose a model before it has seen the answer. The engineering and the theory stay honest there.
